subject: Renewal proposal: velocity-triggered tier migration + phased onboarding credits
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha@orbitai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal proposal: velocity-triggered tier migration + phased onboarding credits

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per follow-up, attached is a concise renewal proposal that shifts OrbitAI from a flat annual commit to a velocity-triggered migration plan. High level: 

- Term: 24 months (co-terming optional at renewal)
- Start: Jan 1, 2027 effective date (can be backdated to invoice start)
- Capacity structure: three-tier ladder (Baseline / Growth / Peak) with automated tranche unlocks tied to observed monthly velocity (see attached schedule).
- Onboarding credits: phased credits (10%, 6%, 4%) that unlock at 30%, 60%, and 90% of committed throughput to de-risk initial traffic and accelerate setup. Credits are applied to invoice as one-time line items.
- Canary policy: short-lived 30-day canary for new high-throughput routes; automatic revert to previous tier if latency/quality regressions exceed thresholds.
- True-up cadence: quarterly true-ups with a one-time annual reconciler.

I included two optional clauses to consider: a sunrise upsize clause (favors early-scale discounts if OrbitAI exceeds Tier 2 for 3 consecutive months) and a smoothing clause for auto-renew (requires 60-day notice to change auto-renew behavior).

Attachments: RW_Renewal_Proposal_OrbitAI_v3.pdf (proposal) and onboard_velocity_schedule.xlsx (milestones & proration examples).

Next steps I suggest:
1) Quick internal review on your side (procurement + engineering) — can you confirm who should be looped in from procurement?
2) If the structure looks good, Jordan will pull a short redline to the SOW and Marissa will confirm billing/proration examples.
3) If accepted, we’ll generate a revised SOW and a single PO-ready invoice.

Happy to run a 30-minute walk-through with your engineering and procurement teams next week. What time looks best?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Appreciate the crisp proposal and the pacing idea. A few quick items from our side:

- Engineering: our infra team will want to review the canary thresholds (SLA/backstop numbers) — I’ll invite them to any walk-through.

Thanks Samantha — great flags. Looping in Jordan (legal) and Marissa (billing) to pick up the redline and proration details. Quick clarifications below so procurement has something to work against: 

- Auto-renew: we can make the 60-day notice firm language in the SOW; we’ll include a 30- to 60-day customer notice window depending on the billing cadence.
- Credits on invoice: Marissa will confirm but our standard is to show credits as separate credit memos (line items) for transparency; workbook includes examples for a Jan start with month-by-month proration.
- Canary thresholds: engineering suggested guardrails in the proposal are 99th-percentile latency delta > 20% or error-rate spike > 2x baseline to trigger rollbacks. We can pass exact signal names to your infra team in the call.

Marissa — can you confirm how the phased-credit memos will display and whether OrbitAI needs a consolidated annual true-up invoice or quarterly reconciliations?

Jordan — if you can draft a brief SOW redline that includes the fixed 60-day auto-renew notice + sunrise upsize clause, that would keep things moving.

Samantha — Tues 11/30 10:00 AM PST or Wed 12/1 9:00 AM PST both work for me for a 30-min walkthrough. Which do you prefer?

Best,
Camila

Thanks Camila / Samantha — I put together a short set of redlines and called out the primary commercial/legal positions: 

1) Auto-renew: accept firm 60-day notice requirement to change renewal behavior; include clear statement that failure to provide notice maintains current renewal behavior (no mid-cycle unilateral changes).
2) Sunrise upsize clause: acceptable with cap — suggest a maximum 15% retroactive discount credit for early-scale months to protect pricing integrity.
3) Data residency / audit: add a short paragraph confirming dataset residency and audit access windows for OrbitAI (required for some regulated customers).
4) Termination / true-up: recommend limiting invoice true-up exposure to one annual reconciler plus quarterly forecasts to avoid unpredictable mid-year cost.

I attached the redline (SOW_Redline_OrbitAI_20261130.docx) to my internal note — Camila, please send to Orbit procurement after you sync with Marissa on PRs.

Jordan Blake
